QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_9

question.text: Subscription and redemption documents for a Cat III open-ended AIF scheme must typically include which of the following investor-facing items?

answer.text: Contribution Agreement, Investor Charter reference, PPM acknowledgment, KYC/FATCA declarations and redemption notice mechanics
Distributor commission schedule and MFN side-letter mandatorily appended
SEBI circular text printed verbatim in full

explanation.text: The Logic: Subscription/redemption documentation for a Cat III open-ended scheme typically bundles: contribution agreement (units issued against subscription price at NAV), Investor Charter reference, PPM acknowledgment, KYC/FATCA/CRS declarations, and redemption notice windows (e.g., T+30 / quarterly gates). These operationalise the governance disclosures. The Trap: Distributor commission schedules are disclosed but not typically appended; MFN side-letters are case-by-case. SEBI circulars are referenced, not embedded. Trustee personal net-worth is not an investor-facing requirement. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B distributors frame these as point-of-sale documents; XIX-E Cat III manager treats them as back-office controls and NAV-linked accounting triggers. Manager's Pro-Tip: For a Cat III open-ended fund with daily NAV and monthly redemption gates, ensure the subscription form captures the investor's election on equalisation-credit vs series-accounting — it drives how HWM crystallisation runs on incentive fees for new investors subscribing mid-year.
